cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. When the land is divided by lot as an inheritance, He says, "…you are to set aside a portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land…" (Ezekiel 45:1). Before anybody gets a slice, friends, a portion is already marked for Him.
The answer is False. Nobody gets to cut this tract into holy parts and ordinary parts. The LORD says, "This entire tract of land will be holy." (Ezekiel 45:1). Every cubit of it counts, friends.

The answer is the priests who minister in the sanctuary. This strip is "…a holy portion of the land to be used by the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to minister before the LORD." (Ezekiel 45:4). It's also a place for their houses. The ones who serve nearest the sanctuary get to live nearby.

The answer is the Levites who minister in the temple. The adjacent area "…shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple…" (Ezekiel 45:5). It's their possession, and the towns where they live go there. Priests on one side, Levites on the other, and the sanctuary right nearby. I'd never have to hunt for a neighbor to borrow a mixing bowl from!

The answer is True. The city's area is set aside beside the holy district, and "It will belong to the whole house of Israel." (Ezekiel 45:6). It isn't only for the priests, the Levites or the prince. The whole house of Israel shares it, friends.

The answer is False. The prince gets his own possession, and that's where it stops. God says His princes "…will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes." (Ezekiel 45:8). No extra helpings for him, friends.

The word is oppress. God says, "…My princes will no longer oppress My people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes." (Ezekiel 45:8). Oppress means pressing down on people who should be looked after. Under this plan, the prince gives land instead of taking it.

The answer is to do what is just and right. God says, "Cease your violence and oppression, and do what is just and right." (Ezekiel 45:9). He doesn't only tell them what to stop, friends. He tells them what to start. And right after that He says, "Stop dispossessing My people…"

The word is honest. God says, "You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath." (Ezekiel 45:10). An ephah and a bath are measures for dry and liquid goods. If I put my thumb on my cookie scale, every box gets lighter and nobody trusts me. God wants measures that tell the truth.

The answer is all the people of the land. The text says, "All the people of the land must participate in this contribution for the prince in Israel." (Ezekiel 45:16). Nobody gets to sit this one out, friends. Everybody brings something to the table.

The answer is to provide the offerings for the feasts. "…it shall be the prince’s part to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths…" (Ezekiel 45:17). He also provides the sin offerings and peace offerings. The people bring the contribution, and the prince makes sure the offerings are there.

The answer is True. The prince will provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings and peace offerings "…to make atonement for the house of Israel." (Ezekiel 45:17). Atonement is the purpose the text names, friends. The offerings are for the whole house of Israel.

The answer is to purify the sanctuary. The Lord GOD says, "…take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary." (Ezekiel 45:18). A young bull without blemish is the offering for it. That's for the first day of the first month.

The answer is False. The offering is done "…for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance." (Ezekiel 45:20). Those are the two cases the text names, friends. In this way atonement is made for the temple.

The answer is the Passover. God says, "On the fourteenth day of the first month you are to observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten." (Ezekiel 45:21). Seven days, with unleavened bread the whole time. That's a long stretch without puffy dough, friends.

The word is people. The prince "…shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land." (Ezekiel 45:22). Notice it's for himself too, friends. He's in the same boat as everybody else.

The answer is the same offerings as at Passover. For the feast that begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, "…he is to make the same provision for sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil." (Ezekiel 45:25). Same list, same amounts. No new recipe to learn, friends.
